reviewerOrPass: Worker A, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: After freezing the pair, returned to the faculty regulations, independently re-added the three 60 EC years and checked Articles 4.2 and 5.3 before reading the finished case. Rechecked the catalogue conflicts and the active workbook for the selected course contents, prerequisite direction, offerings and course reuse. Then compared the independent reconstruction with the frozen decision, canonical record and mapped reader-facing text.
findings: The full-time English Maastricht Computer Science BSc is illustrated using the published 2025–26 regulations. Appendix 1 gives twelve four-credit courses and two six-credit projects in Year 1, ten four-credit courses and two ten-credit modules in Year 2, then six four-credit electives across Blocks 3.1 and 3.2, a six-credit Project 3-1, three four-credit courses and an 18-credit thesis. Counting each semester module and project once gives 60+60+60 EC. Appendix 1 controls formal component names and credits. Use BCS1430 Object-Oriented Modelling instead of the catalogue BCS1450 Computer Architecture and BCS2510 IT Management & Privacy instead of the catalogue year-two Operating Systems. Count Operating Systems once in year three. Year 3 ethics and computation titles follow the Appendix. The year-two modules shown are first in official order. Optional tracks, other-provider credit, the minor and exchange do not add credits to this route.

A standard on-time student can meet Article 4.2 by taking the four stated foundational courses in year one and completing Project 1-2. Module 2-1 and 2-2 each require two of the four named courses and registration for or completion of at least three courses in the respective semester; Module 2-2 also requires Project 1-2. Project 3-1 requires Module 2-1 and at least three Year 3 semester-one courses registered or complete. The exam thresholds in Article 5.3 are 45 EC from Year 1 for Year 2 exams and 60 EC from Year 1 plus 40 EC from Year 2 for Year 3 exams. Thesis application additionally needs 138 EC overall, within reach after the first 150 EC. The modules include skill classes and project attendance, not counted separately. The six elective slots remain open within the formal lists and credit limits. No current-cohort rule is asserted.

The dated formal route includes one 4 EC Operating Systems course and one 18 EC thesis. The workbook confirms two related 24-course options. UCR networks and operating systems share one course, and signal processing and robotics do not provide a high-performance computing sequence or a human-computer interaction studio. The case surfaces the different published listings and the illustrative academic year.
